text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: production sign failures detected - third-party KMS API errors (GCP/AWS) during bootstrap. Paging primary on-call: @Luis (oncall). :rotating_light:

Luis (oncall): seeing a surge of signing errors in the fleet during pod init. New pods stuck at 'fetching keys' step. Error traces show `context deadline exceeded` and `rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded` from cloudkms.googleapis.com and also a handful to kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com.

Jia Kim: metrics: cloudkms rpc p99 spiked from ~200ms -> 7s around 08:12 UTC. Affected clusters: prod-1, prod-2 in us-central1 and eu-west-1. Startup scripts perform ~4 parallel KMS calls for each worker; that will magnify failures.

Tomas V.: customer impact: user traffic still flows on warm instances; however autoscale and rolling deploys are failing. Some customers with rapid scaling patterns may observe delayed capacity. No 5xx errors observed yet on API endpoints.

Luis (oncall): immediate mitigation proposals: (1) enable staggered init (randomized backoff) so we don't thundering herd, (2) switch to local signing proxy for internal telemetry, (3) short circuit non-essential KMS calls on boot. Which is quickest?

Nora Li: I can push a startup hook script that serializes key fetch with exponential backoff + jitter, that needs a deploy but it's a tiny change. Also can add a local /var/cache/kms-dek that init checks first.

Tomas V.: open a support case with cloud provider(s). I will start with GCP Support Case: GCP-2026-0821. Include p99 graphs and sample request IDs.

DeployBot: Rollout queued: patch-startup-stagger v1 -> canary clusters. User: Nora Li.

Luis (oncall): recommendation: canary one cluster with the stagger + cache check and increase KMS call timeout to 15s via env REDWOOD_KMS_RPC_TIMEOUT=15000. Start canary then measure.

Jia Kim: I also created a temporary traffic-control rule on autoscaler to slow down spike scaleups: max-concurrent-startups=2 per node-group. This reduces concurrent KMS calls during a scale event.

Nora Li: canary applied to prod-1; logs show canary pod completed init after 2 retries. Sign success ratio improved from ~80% -> ~98% for the canary.

Tomas V.: GCP Support replied: investigating networking layer in us-central1; they see elevated RPC latencies affecting Cloud KMS for some projects. They've escalated to the control plane team. Case GCP-2026-0821 is active.

Luis (oncall): additional mitigation: spinning up ephemeral signing-broker service inside the VPC that batches and proxies signing requests to KMS at a controlled rate. This would be a short-lived internal service to reduce outbound RPC fanout. Feasible in ~1h?

Jia Kim: I can stand up a minimal signing proxy in 45m (node pool + simple API) that authenticates with our KMS key and accepts internal requests. It will cache DEKs for a TTL and limit concurrency. This reduces external KMS calls by ~70% per init wave. Are we ok with the trust model? Only for internal metrics/telemetry, not for customer encryption keys.

Tomas V.: approved for internal-only usage. Ship it to mitigate. Notify security afterwards for review.

DeployBot: Job job-9922 created: signing-proxy-canary.

Nora Li: proxy deployed in canary, integrated with init hook. Observed reduction in direct KMS RPCs; proxy to KMS calls remain but are rate-limited. Can confirm canary cluster had zero startup timeouts after proxy wired.

Luis (oncall): paging rotation note: I'm keeping the incident open. Handing monitoring to @Tomas V. in 30m. Leave a short summary here please.

Tomas V.: joining provider call with GCP now. Update from GCP: they reported a regional control-plane load spike affecting Cloud KMS; mitigation rolling out and target ETA ~09:05 UTC. They recommend we keep throttles and use retries with jitter.

Jia Kim: we also verified some nodes in eu-west-1 were routed through a misbehaving egress proxy causing increased latency to kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com. Network team is fixing the egress proxy rules. That explains the cross-cloud errors.

Luis (oncall): actions taken so far: - startup hook added to check local DEK cache - staggered init + exponential backoff + jitter - KMS RPC timeout increased to 15s - autoscaler limited concurrent startups - ephemeral signing-proxy for internal use - non-critical services disabled DEK-refresh at boot

Tomas V.: observed sign success rate across clusters improved from 82% -> 99.2% in 35 minutes after mitigations. No customer-facing errors reported.

GCP Support: Update: control plane mitigations progressing, latencies trending down. Will provide final confirmation when fully resolved.

Luis (oncall): preparing handoff to next oncall @Jia Kim in 40m. Please keep watch on the proxy, autoscaler limits, and cloud support cases.

Jia Kim: acknowledged. I'll stay pinned and will escalate if any regression. I'll also draft a customer-facing status note in case we need to communicate delayed scaling.

Tomas V.: follow-ups for postmortem: - permanent DEK cache with secure TTL and renewal flow - add built-in startup backoff with capped concurrency - implement signing-proxy pattern as an on-demand platform feature - update runbooks and comm templates for provider KMS outages - consider multi-region KMS strategy for bootstrapping

IncidentBot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigated -> monitoring. Duration so far: ~28m.

Luis (oncall): closing summary for incident log entry: root cause: third-party KMS control-plane and egress proxy issues causing high RPC latency, affected Cloud KMS APIs in multiple regions; impact: intermittent instance startup failures, delayed autoscaling; mitigations: staggered init, increased timeouts and retries, autoscaler concurrency limits, ephemeral signing-proxy and local DEK cache; status: stable, monitoring. Postmortem owner: Tomas V.

DeployBot: Incident closed: 1792608765. Duration: 00:24:35.

Tomas V.: tagging incident with: kms, third_party, provider_outage, mitigated, postmortem_required

Jia Kim: thanks everyone. I'll put the postmortem draft in /docs/incidents/kms-autoscale-outage-draft and ping for review. :v:
